column1: # Rule: a bilinear read between two texels a and b (16-bit levels) at a fraction f of the way from a's centre to b's:
# the weight is w = round(f 256) (steps of 1/256), the read rounds half up to a 16-bit step:
# (a (256 - w) + b w + 128) >> 8. It holds on 8-bit images too (their texels as 16-bit levels, k 257).
# Source: measurement "Transforms" ("Bilinear reads take weights in steps of 1/256, rounded") and "One-effect projects" >
# "What nodes hold and how they read" ("A read is bilinear with the weight in 1/256ths and rounds half up").
# Tolerance: exact. Ours computes the read in single precision and rounds an exact tie ((a (256 - w) + b w) mod 256 = 128)
# down, where the rule rounds it up: rows 1000/1001, 0/1 and 0/255 at w = 128 show it (ours one level below). Left as it is
# (this table is part of a pure refactor); an implementation should follow rule_16.
# Columns: a_16, b_16 = the two texels; fraction = f; weight_256 = w; ours_16 = our read; rule_16 = the integer form above.
